messages:
maria: FYI I'm drafting a lightweight proposal for an async "handoff" path where we ship full request/response payloads to a secure telemetry sink only when a deterministic sampler marks the call. Want quick feedback before I turn this into an RFC.

Context: hosted API wants deeper traces for regressions without blowing up storage or leaking PII.

---

dave: big ❤️ on getting this right early. immediate concerns: PII boundaries (emails, credit cards, long prompts), retention, and who can ever decrypt. we need a clear redaction-first pipeline.

anika: +1. suggestion: use a stable sampling key derived from customer org id + salted hash so sampling is reproducible per-tenant and auditable. prefer server-side deterministic sampling vs random.

oliver: also add a correlation_id in the runtime headers so the async handoff links back to the original request without including tokens inline. e.g. `x-rwd-cid: <uuid>` and store that in both systems.

maria: sketch of the handoff header we were thinking:
```
x-rwd-cid: uuid-v4
x-rwd-sample-hash: sha256(org-id + salt)
x-rwd-sample-version: v1
```
If sampler decides this call is in-scope, runtime queues the full payload to the secure sink (KMS encrypted).

sre-oncall: cost side: queued full payloads -> storage + egress. need a hard TL;DR quota and per-tenant daily cap. otherwise we'll hit SLO regressions from background upload spikes. also retention TTL must be policy-driven (30/90/365).

product-ops: console gating: fine to surface de-identified traces in product dashboards, but raw payload access should be behind an access request flow with audit logs + JIT approval. auditors/legal will want clear PK/PIA mapping for retention.

dave: on redaction strategy: prefer multi-pass pipeline: 1) token-level masking for known patterns (emails, cc, ssn) using deterministic regex+heuristics, 2) sensitive-field schema redaction for api payloads (e.g., `user.email`), 3) fallback tokenization/hashing for ambiguous text. avoid one-size blanket blackbox redactions because we lose debugging signal.

anika: question about model KV cache: prompt prefixes stored in cache can leak PII. do we redact before caching? or mark cached entries as ephemeral and exclude from telemetry dump? leaning to exclude cached prefixes from telemetry until we have a stronger path.

oliver: for rollout: we should canary on a dedicated internal org first with `sample-version: v1` flagged off for prod. add runtime-config toggle in console that only infra/admins can flip per-region. no global on-by-default.

maria: on hashing/salt lifecycle — propose we sign the sample-hash with a rotating server-side salt stored in Vault; store the salt version in `x-rwd-sample-version`. That lets us rotate without invalidating audit correlation for old records.

product-ops: legal: must support subject-access deletion (GDPR). telemetry sink needs indexable pointers to delete all artifacts for a subject quickly. include that requirement in the RFC.

sre-oncall: ops ask: what about downstream alerting derived from these full payloads? prefer we emit aggregated metrics only to main pipelines and keep raw payloads strictly in the secure sink with limited consumer ACLs.

dave: technical nit: avoid reversible obfuscation. hashing with per-tenant salt + HMAC is fine. but if we ever need to show raw to SRE, that should be done via a secure, audited decrypt path (not plain console).

maria: rough action items I plan to include in the RFC:
- deterministic sampling algorithm (sha256(org_id + salt) % N) + per-tenant cap
- multi-pass redaction ruleset + fallback hashing for free-form text
- explicit disallow list: prompt cache segments excluded from handoff by default
- console ACL + JIT approval for raw payload access + audit trail
- retention/TTL tiers and cost guardrails (quota enforcement)
- canary plan (internal org -> staged rollout)
- GDPR deletion API for telemetry sink

telemetry-bot: Created ticket REDWOOD-ENG-5634: "async log handoff + redaction pipeline" assigned to maria. ETA: 2 weeks for RFC draft.

oliver: +1 to everything above. add a small test harness that replays sampled requests in a sandbox for quality/regression checks (no real tenant perms).

anika: also add unit tests for redaction heuristics and a corpus of synthetic prompts that include edge-case PII. we'll need CI gating before canary.

maria: thanks all — I'll fold these into the RFC. if you have an obvious no-go (e.g. must not ship any raw prompts at all), flag here; otherwise I'll post the RFC early next week. :+1:
